meta.title: Century M11c historical boundary reconstruction and audit, 1 January 1900
meta.method: Modern Natural Earth units are used only as geometric building blocks. Every territorial difference from the modern map is an explicit transfer in `patches`, with dated sources, a confidence class and a note. The map build applies the transfers with polygon-clipping, simplifies to 0.02 degrees and records the resulting provenance on every polity.

confidenceDefinitions.high: Supported by strong historical cartographic, administrative or treaty evidence, with only modern generalization uncertainty.
confidenceDefinitions.medium: Reconstructed from reliable sources; the frontier line or the exact extent has some unresolved uncertainty.
confidenceDefinitions.low: Approximate historical extent where the available evidence is incomplete or the frontier was not surveyed/defined.

geometryClasses.direct-modern-verified: One modern unit whose external border is documented as identical in 1900.
geometryClasses.aggregate-modern-verified: A union of modern units whose combined 1900 external border is documented as identical.
geometryClasses.reconstructed: The 1900 geometry differs from the modern map and is rebuilt with explicit transfers.
geometryClasses.approximate: A defensible but low-confidence historical extent, explicitly not an exact frontier.
geometryClasses.marker-only: No polygon; retained only where no defensible extent can be established.

sourceRegistry.notes: Contemporary description of the German Empire's constituent states and its eastern provinces, including Posen, West Prussia, East Prussia and Silesia.

sourceRegistry.notes: Contemporary description of Ottoman Tripolitania, the vilayet of Tripoli, the sanjak of Benghazi and the Fezzan; used for the Libyan provincial components and the note on limited effective control in the interior.

sourceRegistry.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Darfur'
sourceRegistry.notes: Describes the restored Darfur Sultanate after 1898 and its approximate western Sudanese extent; used for the reconstructed Darfur polygon.

sourceRegistry.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Wadai'
sourceRegistry.notes: Describes Wadai (Ouaddai) in eastern Chad and its dependencies; used for the reconstructed Wadai polygon.

sourceRegistry.title: Hammond's Modern Atlas of the World (1912)
sourceRegistry.notes: Political atlas contemporary with the reference date; cross-check for European, African and Asian external borders.

sourceRegistry.title: The Times Survey Atlas of the World (1920), historical political sheets
sourceRegistry.notes: Cross-check for post-1900 changes; used only where the 1900 border is explicitly marked in the historical sheets.

sourceRegistry.title: Karte Deutsches Reich, Verwaltungsgliederung 1900-01-01 (Wikimedia Commons)
sourceRegistry.notes: Administrative map of the German Empire on the reference date; used to check Alsace-Lorraine, the Prussian eastern provinces, Schleswig-Holstein and the constituent states.

sourceRegistry.title: Reichsgesetzblatt 1871, Treaty of Frankfurt boundary annexations
sourceRegistry.notes: Primary instrument transferring Alsace and the Moselle departments to the German Empire.

sourceRegistry.title: Treaty of Versailles (1919), territorial clauses
sourceRegistry.notes: Used inversely to identify what the German Empire held in 1900: Alsace-Lorraine, Posen, West Prussia, parts of Silesia, Memel, northern Schleswig and Eupen-Malmedy.

sourceRegistry.title: Treaty of Saint-Germain (1919), Austro-Hungarian territorial clauses
sourceRegistry.notes: Used inversely for Galicia, Bukovina, Transylvania, Vojvodina, South Tyrol, Trieste and the Dalmatian coast.

sourceRegistry.title: Treaty of Trianon (1920), Hungarian territorial clauses
sourceRegistry.notes: Used inversely for the Hungarian half of Austria-Hungary, including Transylvania, Slovakia, Vojvodina and Kotor.

sourceRegistry.title: Treaty of Lausanne (1923), Ottoman successor boundaries
sourceRegistry.notes: Used inversely for Ottoman Europe and Anatolia: Kars/Ardahan/Artvin to Russia in 1878, Crete autonomous, and the Balkan/Macedonian provinces still Ottoman in 1900.

sourceRegistry.title: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium Agreement (1899)
sourceRegistry.notes: Defines the Sudan condominium that in 1900 still excluded Darfur.

sourceRegistry.title: ICJ, Territorial Dispute (Libyan Arab Jamahiriya/Chad), Judgment of 3 February 1994
sourceRegistry.license: ICJ public documents; quotation and citation only
sourceRegistry.notes: The Court treated the Anglo-French Declaration of 21 March 1899 as defining a line limiting the French zone or sphere of influence, and the 1919 Convention and 1902 Franco-Italian agreement as later boundary instruments. The 1955 Franco-Libyan Treaty is a post-1900 instrument. The judgment is used here to distinguish a claimed sphere of influence from effective administration on 1 January 1900; no boundary from the later treaty is projected back onto the 1900 map.

sourceRegistry.title: ICJ, Territorial Dispute (Libya/Chad), written pleadings and oral records, 1991-1993
sourceRegistry.notes: Libya and Chad disputed the extent and effectiveness of Ottoman, Senussi, Toubou and French authority in Tibesti, Borkou, Ennedi and the Aouzou strip. The pleadings are used as evidence of contested authority, not as a survey of 1900 administration.

sourceRegistry.title: Labrador boundary dispute and the 1927 Privy Council reference
sourceRegistry.notes: The interior boundary between Quebec and Labrador was disputed around 1900 and was referred to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in 1927. The M11c map uses the modern province outline only as a geometric proxy and does not treat the 1927 line as an uncontested 1900 border.

sourceRegistry.title: Treaty of Petrópolis between Bolivia and Brazil (1903)
sourceRegistry.notes: Bolivia ceded Acre to Brazil after the 1902-03 conflict. The treaty and the subsequent demarcation are post-1900 and are not applied to the 1900 map; Acre is Bolivian in the M11c geometry.

sourceRegistry.title: British Aden and the Aden Protectorate, 1839-1900
sourceRegistry.notes: Aden and its hinterland were British Indian territory in 1900; the Ottoman-Yemeni frontier was not delimited until 1904-1914, so the southern limit is approximate.

sourceRegistry.title: historical-basemaps world_1900 (cross-check only)
sourceRegistry.notes: Used only as a visual and topological cross-check for the German eastern border and the broad extent of the Ottoman Sahara. No coordinate ring from this dataset is redistributed; all final geometry is rebuilt from public-domain modern units and the explicit transfer polygons above.

sourceRegistry.title: CShapes 2.0 (classification reference only)
sourceRegistry.notes: Consulted for status coding only; not used for geometry.

sourceRegistry.title: Century M11c authored boundary reconstruction
sourceRegistry.notes: Explicit transfer polygons, clipping lines and per-polity provenance. Every reconstructed frontier is labelled HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; approximate lines are not presented as exact.

patches.description: Cieszyn (Teschen) Silesia and Bielsko, Austrian until 1918.

patches.description: Kars, Ardahan and Artvin, annexed by Russia in 1878 and Ottoman before that.
patches.notes: The three modern Turkish provinces approximate the 1878-1918 Russian Kars Oblast; the border with the rest of the Ottoman Empire is the 1878 line.

patches.notes: The rectangle approximates the Sanjak's Serbian districts (Novi Pazar, Sjenica, Prijepolje). The 1900 frontier was a military-administrative line, not a modern district border; parts of the rectangle may include Serbian-administered territory.

patches.description: Pljevlja, Bijelo Polje, Berane, Plav and RoÃ…Â¾aje, acquired by Montenegro only in 1912-13.
patches.notes: The five municipalities were Ottoman SandÃ…Â¾ak territory in 1900; the 1912-13 Montenegrin acquisitions are removed.

patches.description: Epirus, Macedonia, Thrace and the North Aegean islands, Ottoman in 1900 and Greek only after the Balkan Wars.
patches.notes: The modern Greek regions are broader than the 1881 Greek-Ottoman frontier. Arta and parts of southern Epirus were already Greek; the whole-region subtraction therefore under-represents Greece by a small strip. LOW confidence applies to the Arta/Ioannina frontier.

patches.description: The Dodecanese islands, Ottoman in 1900 and Italian only from 1912.
patches.notes: The rectangle includes Rhodes, Kos and Karpathos. It is clipped to Greece so the Turkish mainland is unaffected; small islets at the rectangle edge may be missed.

patches.description: Crete, an autonomous Ottoman vassal state under the 1897-98 settlement.
patches.notes: The modern Crete region is the island; it is removed from Greece and assigned to the Cretan State.

patches.description: Southern Dobruja (Dobrich and Silistra), Romanian from 1878 to 1913.
patches.notes: The two modern Bulgarian provinces correspond to the Dobrujan territory Romania held in 1900; Bulgaria acquired it in 1913.

patches.description: Tripolitania, Cyrenaica and Fezzan under Ottoman sovereignty in 1900, minus the Aouzou–Tibesti disputed/no-established-administration zone.
patches.notes: Modern Libya is used as the outer administrative frame. The Ottoman vilayet of Tripoli, the sanjak of Benghazi and the Fezzan were not delimited to modern precision; effective control in the Fezzan and the southern desert was limited and shared with local authorities. The Aouzou–Tibesti zone is excluded from both OTT and FEA and represented as a map-only disputed/no-established-administration area; the 1935 Franco-Italian cession and the 1955 Franco-Libyan treaty are post-1900 and are not applied retroactively.

patches.description: Aden and the southern Yemeni protectorates, British Indian territory in 1900.
patches.notes: The Ottoman-British frontier in Yemen was not delimited until 1904-1914. The modern southern governorates are used as a defensible proxy for the Aden Protectorate and Hadhramaut; the northern limit is approximate.

patches.description: Battambang, Siem Reap, Sisophon, Preah Vihear and Stung Treng, Siamese in 1900 and ceded to France in 1904-07.
patches.notes: The modern Cambodian provinces approximate the western Cambodian provinces under Siamese suzerainty in 1900. The 1904 and 1907 treaties moved the frontier; the exact 1900 line is uncertain.

patches.description: Sainyabuli (Xaignabouli) west of the Mekong, Siamese in 1900.
patches.notes: Only Sainyabuli is reconstructed. Other trans-Mekong districts ceded in 1904-07 are not separated because the modern Lao provinces mix both banks; this under-represents Siam by a small amount.

patches.description: Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis and Terengganu, Siamese vassals in 1900 and transferred to British protection in 1909.
patches.notes: The four modern Malaysian states were under Siamese suzerainty in 1900 under the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909.

patches.description: The Raj of Sarawak, a separate British-protected polity, not part of British Malaya.
patches.notes: Sarawak was ruled by the Brooke dynasty under British protection and was not one of the Malay States. The modern Malaysian state is used as the polygon.

patches.description: Goa, Daman and Diu, Portuguese India in 1900.
patches.notes: Goa and the Daman/Diu union territory are removed from British India and grouped with the Portuguese colonial possessions. The grouping is a map aggregation; Portuguese India was a separate colony.

patches.description: Puducherry, Karaikal, MahÃƒÂ© and Yanam, French India in 1900.
patches.notes: The modern Puducherry union territory is used as the proxy for the four French enclaves. The enclaves are tiny; grouping them with French Indochina is a map aggregation, not an administrative claim.

patches.description: The Maldives, a separate British protectorate, not part of Ceylon.
patches.notes: The Maldives became a British protectorate in 1887 and were not administered as part of Ceylon.

patches.description: Gwadar, an Omani possession on the Makran coast until 1958.
patches.notes: The rectangle approximates the Gwadar enclave; the exact 1900 boundary with British Baluchistan is uncertain.

patches.description: Tibet, an autonomous province under Qing suzerainty, separated from the Qing polygon for map representation.
patches.notes: The Tibet Autonomous Region covers only part of the 1900 Tibetan cultural and administrative sphere; Amdo (Qinghai) and Kham (Sichuan/Yunnan) are not separated. The polygon is a conservative core, not the full Tibetan plateau.

patches.description: The Khanate of Khiva, a Russian protectorate in 1900.
patches.notes: The khanate's irrigated core along the Amu Darya is approximated by Xorazm, Karakalpakstan and DaÃ…Å¸oguz. The desert frontier with Bukhara and Persia was not a hard line.

patches.description: The Emirate of Bukhara, a Russian protectorate in 1900.
patches.notes: The emirate's core (Bukhara, Qarshi, Termez, Dushanbe, Kulob) is approximated by modern Uzbek and Tajik provinces. The eastern Pamir frontier and the desert boundary with Khiva are uncertain.

patches.description: Jabal Shammar (Ha'il), the effective power in northern Najd in 1900; Ottoman sovereignty was nominal.
patches.notes: The emirate's core in 1900 included Ha'il, Qassim and Riyadh after the fall of the Second Saudi State. The Hejaz and al-Hasa remained Ottoman. The desert frontiers are approximate; Ottoman suzerainty over Najd is recorded but not shown as direct administration.

patches.description: Zanzibar and Pemba, a British protectorate, not part of German East Africa.
patches.notes: The five Zanzibar/Pemba regions are removed from German East Africa and grouped with British Indian Ocean possessions. Zanzibar was a protectorate, not a colony.

patches.description: The Kionga triangle, German East Africa until 1919.
patches.notes: The triangle south of the Rovuma mouth is approximated by a small rectangle; the river boundary is generalized.

patches.description: Walvis Bay, a British Cape Colony enclave, not part of German South West Africa.
patches.notes: Walvis Bay was annexed to the Cape in 1884 and surrounded by German territory; the rectangle approximates the enclave.

patches.description: The Volta Region (British Togoland), part of German Togo in 1900.
patches.notes: The Volta Region was the western part of German Togo until the 1914 British occupation; it is removed from the Gold Coast and restored to Togo.

patches.description: British Somaliland, separate from Italian Somaliland in 1900.
patches.notes: The northwest Somali regions are approximated by a rectangle clipped to modern Somalia. The 1894 Anglo-Italian frontier is generalized; Bari and the eastern Sanaag are borderline.

patches.description: Jubaland, British East Africa until 1924, not Italian Somaliland.
patches.notes: The lower and middle Juba provinces and Gedo approximate British Jubaland. The Juba River frontier and the 1900 interior limit are generalized.

patches.description: British New Guinea (Papua), separate from German New Guinea in 1900.
patches.notes: The southern Papuan provinces approximate British New Guinea. The 1885-86 Anglo-German boundary followed the central range, not the modern provincial borders; the split is approximate.

patches.description: The Sokoto Caliphate's core in northern Nigeria, independent until the British conquest of 1900-03.
patches.notes: The caliphate's core emirates are approximated by ten modern Nigerian states. The southern and eastern frontier emirates, Ilorin and the Niger bend are not included; the 1900 border was a shifting military frontier, not a surveyed line.

patches.description: The Wadai (Ouaddai) Sultanate in eastern Chad, independent until the French conquest of 1909-11.
patches.notes: The sultanate's core in OuaddaÃƒÂ¯, Wadi Fira, Batha and the Borkou/Ennedi approaches is approximated by modern Chadian regions. The northern Tibesti and the southern tributary zones are excluded; the frontier was not surveyed.

patches.description: The Darfur Sultanate, restored in 1898 and independent of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan until 1916.
patches.notes: The five modern Darfur states approximate the sultanate's late-19th-century core. The Kordofan frontier and the southern raiding zones are generalized; Darfur's 1900 extent was somewhat larger than the modern states.

patches.description: Acre, Bolivian until the 1903 Treaty of PetrÃƒÂ³polis.
patches.notes: Acre was Bolivian territory in 1900; Brazil acquired it in 1903. The modern state boundary is used.

patches.description: Tacna, under Chilean administration from 1883 to 1929.
patches.notes: Tacna was occupied and administered by Chile after the War of the Pacific; Peru recovered it in 1929. The modern Tacna region is used.

patches.description: Newfoundland and Labrador, a separate dominion in 1900, not part of Canada.
patches.notes: Newfoundland and Labrador were a separate self-governing dominion until 1949. The modern Canadian province is used as the polygon.

patches.description: The Kingdom of Tonga, a British-protected but internally self-governing kingdom, not a British colony.
patches.notes: Tonga was a protected state, not part of the British colonial empire. It is removed from the British Pacific group and given its own polygon.

patches.description: Niue, a British protectorate in 1900 (annexed to New Zealand in 1901).
patches.notes: Niue was not included in any 1900 polity polygon. It is assigned to the British Pacific group; New Zealand's annexation came in 1901.

patches.description: Kerguelen, Crozet, Saint-Paul and Amsterdam islands, French since the 1890s.
patches.notes: The French Southern and Antarctic Lands fill a terrestrial gap in the southern Indian Ocean. They were administered from Madagascar in 1900; grouping them with the French Pacific is a map aggregation.

disputedAreas.name: Aouzouâ€“Tibesti frontier zone
sovereigntyClaims: France: the 21 March 1899 Anglo-French Declaration placed the area in a French sphere of influence; this was not effective administration in 1900.
Ottoman Empire: Tripolitanian claims and later military/administrative activity in the wider Tibesti region; no continuous effective administration across the zone in January 1900.
Local authority: Toubou/Teda communities and trans-Saharan networks exercised the practical authority; no surveyed frontier existed.
disputedAreas.administration: No single power exercised continuous effective administration across the whole zone on 1 January 1900. French posts and columns did not control Tibesti; Ottoman authority was claimed and intermittently projected; local Toubou authority was the most direct administration.
disputedAreas.notes: A cartographic uncertainty zone, not a state. The 1899 declaration is a sphere-of-influence line, not a boundary survey. The 1935 Franco-Italian agreement and the 1955 Franco-Libyan treaty are post-1900 and are not applied retroactively. The rectangle approximates the Aouzou strip (15â€“16Â°E) plus the Tibesti massif (16â€“19Â°E) north of 19.5Â°N, including BardaÃ¯ and Gouro. It is not a precise historical border.

disputedAreas.name: Karakoram–Siachen frontier zone
sovereigntyClaims: British India: Kashmir was a princely state under British suzerainty; its northern boundary was not surveyed in 1900.
Qing China: the Karakoram alignment was not delimited in the Siachen/Aksai Chin sector.
disputedAreas.administration: No surveyed or effectively administered boundary existed in the high Karakoram in 1900. The zone is represented as a disputed frontier rather than assigned to British India or Qing China.
disputedAreas.notes: A small map-only uncertainty zone at the junction of the Karakoram and Siachen. It is not a separate polity and does not change any simulation id. The rectangle is a cartographic proxy for an undelimited high-mountain frontier, not a precise boundary.
